title: The Royal Pin: Collect the Queen
summary: Collect the exposed queen with check, then use a second check to pick up the bishop. Winning material still requires conversion.

nodes.question: The bishop has captured on c5. Should White take the queen?
nodes.explanation: The bishop has left the e5–d6–c7–b8 diagonal. White can capture Qb8 with check. The complete eight-piece root is proved by a legal winning capture into a seven-piece exact Black loss, rather than a direct tablebase query.

branches.title: Independent continuation: a checking fork
commentary: Continue independently after the source capture. The following king replies and queen fork are representative analysis, not a continuation claimed to appear in the clip.
Qxb8+ wins the exposed queen with check; all three black pawns remain part of the exact position.
Kg7 escapes the eighth-rank check. This is one legal defense; ...Ke7 is also available.
Qe5+ checks Kg7 on e5–f6–g7 while attacking Bc5 along the fifth rank. A forcing move lets White improve the material balance again.
Kg6 steps out of check but leaves Bc5 available. This selected reply preserves White’s forced win; it is not presented as the only defense.
Qxc5 removes the bishop. White’s queen and king face three pawns in an exact winning ending, with further conversion still required.

exercises.prompt: Why is taking the queen now legal?
exercises.answer: The black bishop moved from d6 to c5, opening Qe5’s diagonal through d6 and c7 to b8. Qxb8+ also forces Black to answer check.

exercises.prompt: Does the narrator’s warning mean this liquidation is a forced draw?
exercises.answer: No. The warning concerns hasty practical play. The complete position after Qxb8+ is an exact White win with best play, although that does not eliminate the need to convert carefully.

sourceCorrections.claim: The source warns that cashing in too soon is very likely to lead to a draw.
